item.title: A tiny patch could help rescuers perform CPR better; student invention wins $10,000
item.description: Four University of Washington students have developed CPRight, a wallet-sized patch that uses LED lights to guide rescuers during CPR. The device provides real-time feedback on chest compression depth and rate without requiring additional equipment. The invention won the $10,000 undergraduate first prize at the 2026 Collegiate Inventors Competition, which also recognised innovations in cancer treatment, rehabilitation and neurological monitoring. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Así es la rutina ideal para manejar el estrés desde la mañana, sin meditaciones ni mindfulness
item.description: La resiliencia y la flexibilidad psicológica son dos cualidades esenciales para nuestra salud mental, a las que a menudo no prestamos la atención que merecen. Solemos centrarnos en cómo enfrentarnos a las consecuencias del estrés o incluso cómo prevenirlo, pero pasamos de largo sobre el hecho de que a veces, aunque estresarnos sea inevitable, podemos prevenir sus peores consecuencias. Esto, básicamente, es lo que consiguen las personas con buena resiliencia y flexibilidad psicológica. Es algo que puede entrenarse a base de terapia. item.title: Landmark China trial gets 84% efficacy in treating cancer with cue from waste water tech
item.description: For patients with advanced, metastatic cancer that has progressed despite systemic therapy – options remain critically limited. Now, Chinese scientists are pointing to an unconventional therapeutic agent – the element iron. This idea originated in industrial waste water treatment: iron can react with hydrogen peroxide to generate hydroxyl radicals, which degrade various organic and toxic molecules in waste water. Chinese scientists wanted to treat malignant tumours the way they treat waste water... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: New York’s Plaza Hotel to close for four years to restore its historic facade
item.description: Starting in January 2027, New York City's iconic Plaza Hotel will embark on a significant facade restoration that is projected to last a minimum of four years. This closure will impact not only guests but also local residents. With previous renovations totaling $450 million between 2005 and 2008, and a pandemic-related shutdown in 2020, this restoration seeks to uphold the hotel's renowned architectural significance for generations to come.
